This method takes into account the uncertainties in all variables, the presence of outliers in the data, as well as unknown intrinsic scatter in excess of uncertainties.

It is well known that the CO-to-H$_2$ conversion factor depends on metallicity (cite: Wilson1995; Boselli2002; Bolatto2013; Sandstrom2013). The galaxies analyzed in this work are all massive spirals with a similar metallicity range. We thus decided to use a similar conversion factor for all of them.

The WISE3 band is preferred to the WISE4 band at $22\mu$m for its better angular resolution, although the latter is believed to be a better SFR tracer due to less contamination from polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH) emission (cite: Boselli2004).

It is worth noting that interpreting the results from simple bisector and OLS regressions is statistically hard, since a linear slope could even result from a scenario where there is no correlation between a predictor and its response (cite: Isobe1990; Shetty2014).

We address this issue by weighting each line-of-sight measurement by the number of independent measurements that a given galaxy contributes to the overall sample, as also described in (cite: Zabel2020).
